primary_source.paper: Pfau, Merrill & Bowman (2024), "Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models"

trace_source: generated by running vendor/fillerTokens/src/match3.py's Match3.serial_solve() + serial_cot() logic locally (numpy-only reimplementation of the exact algorithm, extracted because the module itself imports torch/transformers at load time), commit cb39af6458b7476ba07f25e89a9c8fd339c1e229, on dimension=3, mod=10, length=6, seed=1 (np.random.default_rng(1)); saved verbatim to tasks/threesum/published_trace.txt
format_description: Each serial-CoT step is one whitespace-delimited token emitted in a fixed schema order after the 'P' marker: three candidate-triple position-index tokens (digit followed by a literal '-', e.g. '4-'), then one raw input digit copied from a single randomly-chosen coordinate of each of those three indexed tuples, then up to (dimension-1) running coordinate-wise sums mod 10 (emission stops at the first nonzero sum, i.e. it lazily proves non-match), ending with a final 'True'/'False' answer token after the 'A' marker.
theory_citation: The classic 3SUM conjecture (Gajentaan & Overmars, 'A class of intersection problems solvable by triangle decomposition', 1995) is a fine-grained SEQUENTIAL TIME lower bound (~n^2, over unbounded/real-valued input) in the comparison/RAM model -- it says nothing about circuit depth or parallelizability. Here dimension and modulus are fixed small constants (d=3, mod=10) and list length n is the only growing knob, so checking one candidate triple is a constant-size mod-10 adder/comparator, and the full decision (OR over the O(n^3) candidate triples) is expressible as a bounded-depth, poly-size threshold circuit family in n -- i.e. TC0 (see e.g. Vollmer, 'Introduction to Circuit Complexity', 1999, ch.4 on threshold circuits for iterated addition/comparison). This matches Pfau/Merrill/Bowman's own empirical result that unstructured filler tokens (parallel-friendly extra compute, not a serial trace) already drive 3SUM length-12 dim-3 accuracy to ~100%, which the paper frames via bounded quantifier-depth of the defining formula (exists i,j,k: sum=0) rather than a need for genuinely serial/recursive computation -- i.e. the opposite signature from an NC1-hard or P-complete task.

notes: Trace: generated fresh rather than pulled from the paper's PDF, by transcribing Match3.serial_solve()/serial_cot() (numpy-only logic) out of vendor/fillerTokens/src/match3.py into a standalone script -- avoids importing the module (which pulls in torch/transformers at import time) while running the exact published algorithm, seeded for reproducibility (seed=1 out of the first ~50 tried, chosen because it is a true instance whose first-examined candidate triple is the real match, giving the shortest clean example: 8 CoT steps before the answer token). Tokenizer results: all three (gemma2 via unsloth/gemma-2-2b mirror since google/gemma-2-2b is gated 401; llama3 via NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B mirror since meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B is gated 401; qwen2 via Qwen/Qwen2-7B, ungated) tokenize the CoT portion ('0- 1- 4- 1 7 2 0 0', with add_special_tokens=False) into 18 tokens, so tokens_per_step is identical (2.25) across all three -- each single mod-10 digit is exactly one token in all three vocabularies (confirmed by direct single-string encode checks), but the leading space before each digit is itself a separate token ('_'/'Ġ' whitespace-marker token) and the '-' index-suffix is a second token, so state_atomic_tokens=true refers specifically to the digit/value symbol, not the full ' N-' or ' N' step substring. state_bits = log2(10) (~3.32) reflects the mod-10 value space that the digit-reveal and running-sum steps track; the index-reveal steps ('0-','1-','4-') separately encode a position in [0,n) needing ~log2(n) bits, which is why state_bounded is set false overall: the position-tracking component of this published serial format necessarily grows with list length n even though the value/sum component stays fixed at log2(10) bits -- this was flagged as an open design question in phase-1 desk.json and is now resolved against the actual published format we ran. theory_class judgment call: distinguished the classic 3SUM CONJECTURE (a sequential time lower bound, irrelevant here since dimension/modulus are fixed constants) from the circuit complexity of this fixed-parameter decision problem, which is embarrassingly parallel (OR over independently-checkable candidate triples) and lands in TC0/'solvable', consistent with the paper's own filler-token result (unstructured parallel compute already suffices for ~100% accuracy at length 12). published_data confidence: Table 1 (2SUM-Transform) numbers are high confidence (read directly from a literal results table via WebFetch in phase 1); the Figure 2 (~66%/100%) and Figure 5 (dimension-6 crossover) numbers are MEDIUM confidence -- they were paraphrased out of an automated HTML/text extraction pass over the arXiv page in phase 1, not read off the actual PDF figure images, and should be re-verified against the PDF before being used to grade any replication.
